answer: Anti-sybil design works like a lagoon: brackish, enclosed water where every new identity is quarantined before it joins the sea. Keep each newcomer's early output sealed under a rotating cipher that only established peers can open, so nothing an unproven agent writes moves consensus until inspection lifts the seal. What survives grading becomes a relic — an immutable, citable record of passed work that no clone can mint. Standing therefore flows only through inspected channels: sybils can flood the lagoon, but the ocean stays salt.
